patterns.what_worked: Read-only sweeps of the FrameXML mirror over five origin/-qualified branches, then re-derived every prior-audit claim from source instead of trusting it. That is what surfaced the two corrections the prior audit most needed: the classic family has a SECOND global GetAppropriateTooltip definition (Blizzard_SharedXML/Classic/SharedUIPanelTemplates.lua:759 era), and Blizzard_SharedXMLGame/Tooltip/TooltipDataHandler.lua is tagged [ExcludeLoadGameType vanilla] in the TOC, so on classic_era the secure-dispatch machinery is not loaded at all rather than merely unwired. The whole-tree HookScript census (18 sites classic_era, 40 forever, 29 live) made the Blizzard_PTRFeedback finding conclusive rather than suggestive: its .toc carries OnlyBetaAndPTR: 1 on all five branches, so a release build has no Blizzard code in the shared tooltip's script chain.
patterns.what_was_hard: The brief's Q5 premise is false for the classic family - GameTooltipMixin:SetUnit does not exist on any classic branch, and GameTooltip:SetUnit is an engine method with no Lua definition anywhere in the tree. Answering the question as asked required saying so and re-deriving what actually runs. The three same-named duplicate definitions on the classic tree (GetAppropriateTooltip, GameTooltip_AddErrorLine, GameTooltip_SetDefaultAnchor) also mean no grep for 'the' definition is safe. The mirror's HEAD had to be distinguished from the TacoTip repo's HEAD when validating that nothing was changed.
patterns.skill_gap: Verifying an absence claim rigorously needs two independent sweeps (whole tree AND generated API docs) per branch, and the two duplicate-definition cases show that a single-file grep is not enough to establish 'where is X defined'.
